thread.title: New Ohio law adjusts cutoff date for starting kindergarten - NewsBreak
thread.title_full: New Ohio law adjusts cutoff date for starting kindergarten - NewsBreak

author: Rex Smith
title: New Ohio law adjusts cutoff date for starting kindergarten - NewsBreak
text:
By Rex Smith ,
6 hours ago
CLEVELAND (WJW) – A recently passed Ohio law, HB 114, will officially take effect in March and have an impact on the 2026-2027 school year.
Previously, school districts could choose either August 1 or Sept. 30 to be the cutoff date for a child to have to be five years old and be eligible for kindergarten enrollment.
‘Always be a second home’: Darius Garland leaves heartfelt message for Cleveland The new law will now make the cutoff to be five by whatever the school district’s first day of school is.
HB 114 was authored by State Rep. Adam Bird, (R) New Richmond.
Bird told FOX 8 that he was receiving complaints from his constituents about the old setup. Mainly from people who lived in a district where the cutoff was August 1 and their child turned five shortly after, meaning they’d have to wait an additional year to officially start school.
“The fact that it was an either-or type of situation was very frustrating to constituents, so in order to bring clarity to the situation, we ended up saying whatever school district you live in, it’s the first day of school. That’s when you have to turn five by,” Bird said.
‘Not the end’: Beloved Red Chimney Restaurant in Slavic Village is moving after fire Bird said the new law doesn’t change any of the previous policies for four-year-olds getting an early entry into kindergarten. That process is still dictated by each individual school district.
“All school districts have an early entrance policy, and it typically involves testing and so if you can test and if you can test successfully, you can still be admitted early under that school district’s policy,” he said.
